items.title: SEO News Roundup (March 16 to 23, 2026)
items.summary: Google is developing an opt-out for generative AI in search and integrating Gemini into Chrome for direct answers without clicks. AI tests rewrite page titles to match intent, and commerce expands with cart support. Local SEO faces challenges like low call button usage, multi-location overlap, and HTTPS migration risks.

items.title: AEO and GEO Are Not Just SEO: Build Content Ecosystems for AI Discovery
items.summary: Mike King warns that dismissing AEO and GEO as rebranded SEO risks losing relevance, as AI uses retrieval augmented generation evaluating consensus across Reddit, YouTube, PR, and more. Traditional site-focused SEO falls short for synthetic queries. Marketers must audit formats and build ecosystems linking to a podcast episode.

items.title: The Old SEO Game Is Over: GEO and Search Everywhere Optimization
items.summary: AI like Google Overviews and ChatGPT answer directly, decoupling impressions from clicks with AI traffic up 357% but CTR down 4x. GEO optimizes for AI citations via structure, E-E-A-T, and unique data; Search Everywhere targets TikTok, Reddit, etc. 2026 wins with proprietary insights and human content.

items.title: 93% AI Searches End Without Visits: GEO/AEO Changes This Month
items.summary: 93% of AI sessions avoid sites; traditional SEO dead, GEO/AEO prioritize citation confidence with structured, factual content under 40 words. Traditional volume drops 25%, AI Overviews in 25% searches up 57%, AI referrals up 527%. Adapt to own discovery or pay more for fewer clicks.

items.title: Hachette Pulls 'Shy Girl' After AI Detection Flags
items.summary: Hachette Book Group canceled the US release of horror novel 'Shy Girl' by Mia Ballard following online accusations of AI-generated content. The author claims a freelance editor inserted AI text without her knowledge during formatting. This marks a significant precedent in publishing amid rising concerns over AI in writing.

items.title: Concerns Over Hachette Acquiring Obvious AI-Generated Book
items.summary: Speculative horror author Z.T. Fairfax highlights that 'Shy Girl' showed clear signs of AI writing when self-published yet was acquired by Hachette. The book was released in the UK by the publisher despite the issues. This raises questions about editorial standards in detecting AI content.

items.title: Rachel Rooney's Children's Book Vilified for Traditional Body Positivity Message
items.summary: Transgender Trend shares details on a children's book emphasizing that kids are perfect as they are, valuing their natural body sense. Author Rachel Rooney was labeled a bigot and danger to children for this stance. The post underscores backlash against traditional messaging in children's literature.

items.title: Publisher Cancels Horror Novel's Release Over AI Claims
items.summary: BBC covers Hachette's decision to cancel the release of 'Shy Girl', a BookTok sensation self-published earlier. The pullback follows claims of AI involvement in the writing. This is described as a harrowing tale that became a buzz amid the scandal.

items.title: Novel Pulled From Shelves After Author Accused of Using AI
items.summary: Futurism details the pulling of 'Shy Girl' after AI accusations, questioning future policies on AI disclosure for major deals. The article notes the ongoing AI boom and its impact on publishing. Authors may need to prove human authorship upfront.

items.title: Chappell Roan Controversy: Security Guard Incidents with Young Fan
items.summary: Chappell Roan is facing public backlash after her security team allegedly yelled at and threatened an 11-year-old fan, soccer star Jorginho's daughter, during a breakfast meet-and-greet. The girl's mother, Catherine Harding, shared her account via video, prompting further discussion. Roan apologized, but Rio's mayor banned her from a music event amid the uproar.

items.title: Damon Lindelof Addresses 'Lanterns' Green Lantern Color Controversy
items.summary: Damon Lindelof responded to backlash from comic fans and writer Grant Morrison over his past joke calling the Green Lantern's green color 'stupid.' He admitted being 'sloppy and careless' and apologized while affirming his commitment to the HBO series. The statement came amid production updates on the show.

items.title: John Lithgow Almost Quit HBO 'Harry Potter' Over J.K. Rowling Backlash Fears
items.summary: John Lithgow revealed he nearly declined the role of Dumbledore in HBO's Harry Potter series due to potential backlash tied to J.K. Rowling's views. He expressed concerns about future interviews and public perception. Despite hesitation, he chose to join the project.

items.title: Catherine Harding Details Chappell Roan Security Encounter in Viral Video
items.summary: Pop Base shared a video from Catherine Harding recounting the incident where Chappell Roan's security allegedly harassed her 11-year-old daughter over a fan interaction. The post amplified the family's perspective amid widespread online reaction. It contributed to memes and calls for accountability.

items.title: Damon Lindelof Calls Green Lantern Joke 'Dumb' After Fan Backlash
items.summary: ScreenTime reported Damon Lindelof admitting his joke about Green Lanterns was 'dumb' following criticism from fans and Grant Morrison. He apologized and highlighted his honor in working on the series. The post included promotional images sparking further discussion.

items.title: Conan O'Brien Roasts Timothée Chalamet's Opera Controversy at Oscars
items.summary: DiscussingFilm highlighted Conan O'Brien's Oscars monologue joke about Timothée Chalamet's ballet/opera feud, quipping on security fears from those communities. The timely humor referenced Chalamet's recent controversy. It received strong engagement during awards coverage.

items.title: HubSpot and Intuit Emerge as Potential AI Winners in Tough SMB B2B Landscape
items.summary: BuccoCapital argues that despite sell-offs in SMB software, HubSpot (HUBS) and Intuit (INTU) hold strong moats from scale, data aggregation, and SMB sales expertise, positioning them for AI-driven growth. AI agents will thrive on their full platforms with clean data, benefiting less tech-savvy users, while enabling cheap feature rollouts. An AI-fueled explosion in small business creation further bolsters their prospects.

items.title: Just 5% of SMBs Paying for AI Tools Despite Adoption Hype
items.summary: Affiniti data on SMBs generating $14B+ annual revenue reveals only 5% spend on AI products like ChatGPT (10x more used than Claude), Scribe, Grammarly, and others. This challenges narratives of rapid AI disruption in small business. Silicon Valley overlooks this vast untapped market beginning its AI journey.

items.title: Top AI Tools Small Businesses Must Use in 2026 for Efficiency and Growth
items.summary: Practical AI tools like Intercom, Zendesk for customer support; ChatGPT, Jasper, Canva for marketing; Zapier, ClickUp for automation; Power BI, Zoho for insights; QuickBooks, Vic.ai for finance; and Darktrace, CrowdStrike for security are transforming SMB operations. These integrate easily to automate tasks, reduce costs, and enable data-driven decisions without large teams. In 2026, strategic AI adoption gives small firms a competitive edge.

items.title: Teams Quietly Replacing SaaS with Custom AI Builds, Impacting Business Efficiency
items.summary: A Retool survey shows 35% of teams have replaced SaaS functionality with self-built AI tools, 78% plan more in 2026, often outside IT. AI slashes development costs from weeks to days, targeting niche workflows like approvals and dashboards. For small businesses, this democratizes custom solutions, cutting subscriptions while raising shadow IT risks.
